title: Microburst timeline entropy: latency synthesis and sampling notes
content:
Purpose
- Capture and reason about short-lived microburst arrival patterns that cause transient drops in achieved IPC and sudden tail-latency spikes.
- Explore timeline entropy as a measurable signal (kernel start jitter, inter-kernel quiet windows, async-copy bursts) and tie it to mitigation strategies in the batcher / handoff layer.

Quick summary of findings (tl;dr)
- We see recurring ~200-400us microbursts where SM occupancy briefly collapses despite overall high utilization reported at 1s resolution.
- The entropy metric (stddev of kernel-start deltas per 10ms window) spikes before tail latency increases. This looks like a leading indicator.
- Primary root causes observed: batcher handoff jitter, CUDA-graph fragmentation causing extra host->device enqueue gaps, and occasional DMA contention on NVLink when concurrent copy windows align.

Experiment setup
- HW: H100 (4x per node), NVLink fully enabled, host: c5n.large-ish for trace controller.
- Model: 7B decoder-only transformer (quantized), typical seq_len=512, generation temperature 0.0 for deterministic timing.
- Workload shape: synthetic poisson arrivals tuned to produce bursts; separate runs with real production traffic replay (sample from 2026-06-01 window).
- Capture: Nsight Systems 2026.2 - timeline sampling @ 5us resolution, NVTX annotated traces from batcher + router + kernel entry points. Additional power/clock telemetry dumped every 1ms via nvml.
- CUDA graph capture: enabled for decoder loop, but we also ran variants WITHOUT graphing to compare fragmentation effects.

Key metrics collected
- kernel_start_delta distribution (per-stream)
- kernel_duration_kernal (per-call)
- SM_active_warps / SM_max_warps (instant) sampled at 5us
- warp_stall_reasons breakdown (mem, sync, pipe) aggregated by microburst window
- nvlink_dma_throughput (MB/s) and PCIe fallback events
- GPU_clock / GPU_power time-series sampled 1ms
- entropy_signal = rolling_stddev(kernel_start_delta, window=10ms)

Representative trace notes (run A, production replay)
- 00:00:01.123: spike in entropy_signal -> from 0.8us to 145us stddev. Within next 900us tail latency p95 increases x3.
- NVTX shows: batcher enqueue defers due to lock contention for ~120us, then a flurry of 6 small kernels launched back-to-back. Kernel durations short (~40-70us) but launcher spacing irregular.
- Nsight shows short inter-kernel quiet windows of 30-80us where SM utilization drops to 10-15% (not a full idle, but many warps stalled).
- Warp stall breakdown during burst: mem-bound rises from 38%->64%, sync stalls increase slightly. IPC drops 22% compared to steady-state.

What we think is happening
- Small, irregular batches (microbatches) lead to many short kernels. CUDA graphs try to compact but when graphs are re-created/fragmented on-the-fly (due to dynamic sequence length or cache invalidation) we get host-side scheduling gaps. Those gaps align across streams and create transient DMA/SM underutilization.
- The batcher handoff uses a single atomic queue in the hot path; when contention happens, enqueues stall briefly and then flush, creating the observed microburst shape.
- NVLink DMA overlaps copies with kernel execution normally, but if many copies start in-phase across contexts, NVLink becomes a bottleneck and memory-related warp stalls rise.

Comparison of capture modes
- With CUDA graphs pinned and reused (no recompile/recreate): entropy_signal mean drops ~3x, tail latency p99 improves ~18%.
- Without graphs: more consistent kernel_start_deltas (surprisingly) because the runtime avoids short-lived capture overhead; however overall CPU-side load is higher.
- With aggressive batching (increase microbatch to 2x tokens): occupancy increases but end-to-end latency for single small requests worsens. Tradeoff space confirmed.

Short checklist of plausible mitigations tested locally
- Batcher: move from single atomic queue to sharded handoff with per-worker buffers (reduced enqueue stall in trace by ~70%).
- Handoff smoothing: introduce 100us jitter-smoothing window (coalesce small jobs arriving within window) -> reduces entropy spikes but increases median by ~20us.
- CUDA graphs: enforce persistent pre-created graph library for canonical sequence lengths; fallback path still exists but we avoid re-create churn.
- Stream priority: promote generation kernels to high priority stream to reduce preemption in busy multi-tenant nodes. Observed small improvement in burst recovery time.

Open questions / hypotheses to validate
- Is NVLink contention across GPUs (multi-GPU KV cache coherence) a larger contributor than host-side enqueue jitter? Need multi-GPU cross-node traces.
- How much does model quantization variance (different code paths) cause graph re-creation? We saw graph churn correlate with rare seq_len tails.
- Can a lightweight persistent kernel (single kernel serving many short sequences via internal scheduler) eliminate most microburst pain? Prototype suggestion: persistent decoder kernel that processes a tiny queue on-GPU.

Action items (who / when)
- Liam: prototype sharded enqueue + metrics (ENG-2197) — target: spike free runs on replay by 2026-07-08.
- Jordan: create persistent graph pre-warm for top-5 sequence lengths + add telemetry hooks for graph create events — due 2026-06-30.
- Priya: run multi-GPU NVLink contention sweep (vary concurrent copy alignments) and capture traces — due 2026-07-05.
- Maya: add entropy_signal calculation into dev console and create alert rule (threshold: 50us rolling stddev) — due 2026-07-02.

Notes for reproducibility
- Nsight CLI flags used: nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --sample=us --sample-interval=5us --output=runA.nsys
- NVML poller: python tool polling every 1ms, written to csv with timestamps aligned to nsight via host clock sync script (check github PR for sync helper).
- Synthetic generator: poisson_burst.py (repo/tools/load-gen) using seed 20260614. Replays stored in s3://redwood-traces/microburst/2026-06-14/ runA*.json

Attachments / links
- Trace: s3://redwood-traces/microburst/2026-06-14/runA.nsys (large)
- Jira: ENG-2197 (batcher handoff refactor)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842 (sharded-queue prototype)

Misc rough notes / scribbles
- observed: short kernel storms often follow a 2-3 failed cache-lookup for KV prefetch -> proposal: early-staged cache-deny path that forces small backoff instead of immediate enqueue.
- think about: gating graph re-create behind a soft quota to avoid oscillation during tail seq lengths.

Conclusion
- Microburst-induced entropy is a real signal we can measure cheaply and use as an early-warning for tail latency. Simple engineering changes in the handoff layer + pragmatic use of CUDA graphs (pre-warm / reuse) yield large wins. Next step is multi-GPU validation and the persistent-kernel prototype.

-- Maya
